sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是 Benjamin Poulin，我是 Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店里当 DJ 时，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带上 300 件最珍贵的藏品去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》吧。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的 Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《The Daily》。

sentences.en: Today, the president threatens North Korea with fire and fury and says the country best not make any more threats to the United States.
sentences.zh: 今天，总统威胁朝鲜称要让其见识“烈火与愤怒”，并表示朝鲜最好不要再对美国发出任何威胁。

sentences.en: And for the first time, scientists in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而且，美国科学家首次

sentences.en: have edited the DNA of human embryos to prevent a fatal disease.
sentences.zh: 编辑了人类胚胎的 DNA 以预防一种致命疾病。

sentences.en: Why American law may block the biggest medical breakthrough in decades.
sentences.zh: 为什么美国法律可能会阻碍几十年来最大的医学突破。

sentences.en: Peter Baker, you're in Bedminster, New Jersey with the president.
sentences.zh: Peter Baker，你现在正和总统一起在新泽西州的贝德明斯特。

sentences.en: Take us through this remarkable verbal escalation between the president and North Korea over the course of the day.
sentences.zh: 请带我们了解一下今天总统与朝鲜之间这场惊人的言语升级。

sentences.en: Well, tensions have been building with North Korea, of course, for weeks and months.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，与朝鲜的紧张局势已经持续了数周甚至数月。

sentences.en: Just last month, it tested for the first time an intercontinental ballistic missile that can actually strike the continental United States.
sentences.zh: 就在上个月，它首次试射了一枚实际上可以打击美国本土的洲际弹道导弹。

sentences.en: The U.N.
sentences.zh: 联合国

sentences.en: responded over the weekend with new sanctions.
sentences.zh: 在周末以新的制裁措施作出了回应。

sentences.en: And North Korea said today that it was going to respond with physical action to those who were trying to stop it from building its program.
sentences.zh: 而朝鲜今天表示，将对那些试图阻止其发展计划的人采取实际行动。

sentences.en: Now, that was taken as a threat.
sentences.zh: 这被视为一种威胁。

sentences.en: And so when President Trump was asked about North Korea today, he responded with a threat of his own.
sentences.zh: 因此，当特朗普总统今天被问及朝鲜问题时，他以自己的威胁作出了回应。

sentences.en: And his language is pretty stark.
sentences.zh: 他的措辞非常严厉。

sentences.en: North Korea best not make any more threats to the United States.
sentences.zh: 朝鲜最好不要再对美国发出任何威胁。

sentences.en: They will be met with fire and fury like the world has never seen.
sentences.zh: 他们将面临世界从未见过的烈火与愤怒。

sentences.en: He has been very threatening beyond a normal statement.
sentences.zh: 他的言辞非常具有威胁性，超出了正常的声明范畴。

sentences.en: And as I said, they will be met with fire, fury and, frankly, power, the likes of which this world has never seen before.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，他们将面临烈火、愤怒，坦率地说，还有这个世界从未见过的力量。

sentences.en: That's quite a phrase.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个很有力的措辞。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Very evocative, of course, of a potential nuclear holocaust and the kind of phrase we haven't really heard from presidents.
sentences.zh: 当然，这很容易让人联想到潜在的核浩劫，这是我们以前从未从总统口中听到的那种措辞。

sentences.en: It's actually more common to the kind of language that North Koreans themselves tend to use when they're making bellicose statements.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这更像是朝鲜人在发表好战声明时倾向于使用的那种语言。

sentences.en: But in this case, the president decided to meet fire with fire, or in this case, fire and fury with fire and fury.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，总统决定以火还火，或者说，以烈火与愤怒回击烈火与愤怒。

sentences.en: And, Peter, how did North Korea respond to that language?
sentences.zh: 那么，Peter，朝鲜对这种言论有何回应？

sentences.en: They didn't back off, that's for sure.
sentences.zh: 他们肯定没有退缩。

sentences.en: They issued their own statement basically saying that they would encircle the American military base in Guam in fire.
sentences.zh: 他们发表了自己的声明，基本上说他们将用烈火包围美国在关岛的军事基地。

sentences.en: They like this phrase, fire.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢“烈火”这个词。

sentences.en: It's a phrase they use again today.
sentences.zh: 这是他们今天再次使用的词汇。

sentences.en: And their message is they're not going to back off.
sentences.zh: 他们传达的信息是他们不会退缩。

sentences.en: They say if the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们说如果美国

sentences.en: thinks it's the only one that can wage preemptive war, it's fooling itself.
sentences.zh: 认为只有它能发动先发制人的战争，那它就太自欺欺人了。

sentences.en: In fact, the United States is no longer a heavenly kingdom, it said, immune from other countries' ballistic missiles.
sentences.zh: 事实上，美国不再是一个不受他国弹道导弹影响的天堂之国了，它是这么说的。

sentences.en: It was a pretty stark threat.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当严厉的威胁。

sentences.en: And just to be clear, that is a threat of some kind of attack on an American territory, whether nuclear or non-nuclear, and it seems rather specific.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，这是一种针对美国领土的某种攻击威胁，无论是核攻击还是非核攻击，而且看起来相当具体。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a specific island.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个具体的岛屿。

sentences.en: It's a very specific threat, a very specific island.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常具体的威胁，针对一个非常具体的岛屿。

sentences.en: And it was followed up with the idea that, look, our ballistic missiles are now pointing at the Pacific, and you should look at how far we can launch them, meaning, presumably,
sentences.zh: 随后他们还表示，看，我们的弹道导弹现在正瞄准太平洋，你们应该看看我们能发射多远，这意味着，大概是，

sentences.en: the continental United States.
sentences.zh: 美国本土。

sentences.en: Peter, do you know why North Korea is threatening Guam in particular?
sentences.zh: Peter，你知道为什么朝鲜特别威胁关岛吗？

sentences.en: It's not a territory a lot of us think too much about.
sentences.zh: 那不是我们很多人会过多考虑的领土。

sentences.en: Is it simply because it happens to be within range and nearby and kind of small, or what?
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为它恰好在射程范围内，离得近，而且比较小，还是什么原因？

sentences.en: Well, Guam is actually a very strategic place for us.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关岛对我们来说实际上是一个非常具有战略意义的地方。

sentences.en: It's the place where we have a very key Air Force base, and we've used it over the years to station nuclear bombers, for instance, in the old days.
sentences.zh: 那里有我们一个非常关键的空军基地，过去我们曾用它来驻扎核轰炸机，例如在过去。

sentences.en: And we have used it recently, I think, to fly some strategic planes out of there over the Korean Peninsula to kind of, you know, show force.
sentences.zh: 我想我们最近也用它来派遣战略飞机飞越朝鲜半岛，以展示武力。

sentences.en: So it's a place where if there was war in the Korean Peninsula, this would be where a lot of the reinforcements,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果朝鲜半岛发生战争，这里将是许多增援部队的所在地，

sentences.en: this would be a lot of the projection of American power would come from.
sentences.zh: 这将是美国大部分力量投射的来源地。

sentences.en: Peter, you mentioned these sanctions that the UN passed over the weekend against North Korea.
sentences.zh: Peter，你提到了联合国周末通过的针对朝鲜的制裁措施。

sentences.en: How big a deal are those, and what do they do?
sentences.zh: 这些制裁有多重要，它们有什么作用？

sentences.en: Well, they're a big deal mostly in the fact that it was a unanimous vote, 15 to 0.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们之所以重要，主要是因为这是一次 15 比 0 的一致投票。

sentences.en: Both China and Russia, which have often resisted these kinds of sanctions, decided to go along with it.
sentences.zh: 中国和俄罗斯这两个经常抵制此类制裁的国家，这次决定随大流。

sentences.en: But this is the eighth time the United Nations Security Council has passed sanctions on North Korea.
sentences.zh: 但这已经是联合国安理会第八次通过对朝鲜的制裁了。

sentences.en: And there's no real sense that it would necessarily make a difference unless China is very serious about it.
sentences.zh: 除非中国非常认真地对待，否则没有真正的迹象表明这一定会产生什么影响。

sentences.en: The sanctions said basically that member nations can't import a whole lot of products from North Korea.
sentences.zh: 制裁基本上规定成员国不得从朝鲜进口大量产品。

sentences.en: That could, in fact, crimp the North Korean economy pretty seriously.
sentences.zh: 这实际上可能会严重打击朝鲜经济。

sentences.en: But what we don't know is, of course, what China's real response will be.
sentences.zh: 但我们不知道的是，中国真正的反应会是什么。

sentences.en: Even though they supported it, they've often in the past not genuinely enforced them in the kind of way the United States believes it should.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们支持了制裁，但过去他们往往没有按照美国认为应该的方式真正执行。

sentences.en: But we've wanted China for years to put pressure on North Korea, and they have often said, yes, yes, we agree.
sentences.zh: 但多年来我们一直希望中国对朝鲜施压，而他们经常说，是的，是的，我们同意。

sentences.en: And then in the end, they really haven't, at least not in the way that's changed North Korea's behavior.
sentences.zh: 但最终，他们并没有真正做到，至少没有以改变朝鲜行为的方式做到。

sentences.en: President Trump had a good relationship he forged, it seemed like, at first with President Xi Jinping and Mar-a-Lago.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统起初似乎与习近平主席在海湖庄园建立了一种良好的关系。

sentences.en: But lately, he's been expressing more disappointment that China hasn't sort of followed through.
sentences.zh: 但最近，他表达了更多的失望，因为中国没有落实到位。

sentences.en: And Peter,
sentences.zh: 还有 Peter，

sentences.en: all this seems to be unfolding with a almost monthly test by North Korea of its ballistic missiles and a revelation each time of how much further it seems these missiles can go.
sentences.zh: 这一切似乎都在朝鲜几乎每月一次的弹道导弹试验中展开，而且每次都揭示了这些导弹似乎能飞得更远。

sentences.en: So at this point, how far along is North Korea in its missile development?
sentences.zh: 那么在这一点上，朝鲜的导弹发展到了什么程度？

sentences.en: Well, it's now tested twice, an intercontinental ballistic missile that, in theory, at least, has the range to reach deep inside the United States territory, to Denver, to Chicago,
sentences.zh: 嗯，它现在已经两次试射了洲际弹道导弹，理论上至少有射程深入美国领土，到达丹佛、芝加哥，

sentences.en: and perhaps even further.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能更远。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It has really, I think, taken American analysts and other analysts in the region a little bit by surprise.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实让美国分析人士和该地区的其他分析人士感到有些惊讶。

sentences.en: For years, they've been testing missiles without a lot of success.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他们一直在进行导弹试验，但并没有取得多大成功。

sentences.en: Now they seem to be actually jumping forward with great speed and a speed that's going to genuinely challenge the United States to figure out what to do at this point.
sentences.zh: 现在他们似乎正在以极快的速度向前跨越，这种速度将真正挑战美国，迫使我们思考此时该怎么办。

sentences.en: And finally, Peter, it feels like there have been so many of these escalations with North Korea, and that inevitably they seem to kind of peter out.
sentences.zh: 最后，Peter，感觉与朝鲜的升级事件已经发生了很多次，而且不可避免地，它们似乎都会逐渐平息。

sentences.en: But given the nature of the language used by both sides today and just how amped up it was, and given where North Korea's technology with missiles is, does this feel different?
sentences.zh: 但考虑到今天双方所用语言的性质以及这种激烈的程度，再加上朝鲜导弹技术的现状，这感觉有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: Or is this just another kind of rhetorical battle?
sentences.zh: 还是这只是又一场口水战？

sentences.en: It does feel different.
sentences.zh: 确实感觉不同。

sentences.en: It does feel like we have entered into a new stage.
sentences.zh: 确实感觉我们已经进入了一个新的阶段。

sentences.en: Now, what the stage will be, what it will end up meaning, very hard to say.
sentences.zh: 至于这个阶段会是什么，最终意味着什么，很难说。

sentences.en: But you're right.
sentences.zh: 但你是对的。

sentences.en: There has been sort of a policy for years, particularly under President Obama, of sort of like, let's just ignore North Korea in a public way.
sentences.zh: 多年来，特别是在奥巴马总统任期内，有一种政策，就是公开层面忽略朝鲜。

sentences.en: Let's not give them a lot of attention, which is what they want.
sentences.zh: 不要给他们太多关注，这正是他们想要的。

sentences.en: And then through other means, through subterfuge, through sabotage, try to prevent them from making much progress on their program.
sentences.zh: 然后通过其他手段，通过诡计、通过破坏，试图阻止他们在计划上取得太大进展。

sentences.en: And for years, that seemed to basically keep North Korea in something of a diplomatic box.
sentences.zh: 多年来，这似乎基本上把朝鲜限制在某种外交框架内。

sentences.en: But it didn't solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有解决问题。

sentences.en: And at some point, obviously, that bill is going to come due.
sentences.zh: 在某个时候，显然，这笔账迟早要算。

sentences.en: Now, you know, the question is, is it coming due now under President Trump?
sentences.zh: 现在，你知道，问题是，这笔账现在在特朗普总统任期内要算了吗？

sentences.en: Peter, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: Peter，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Hey, thanks very much.
sentences.zh: 嘿，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Good talking to you, as always.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，很高兴和你交谈。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是 Andrew Ross-Sorkin。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: Vance、Elon Musk、Christine Lagarde、Zoran Mondani 等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在 11 月 18 日在 nytimes.com 上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: You never know when your heart might fail you with this disease.
sentences.zh: 你永远不知道你的心脏什么时候会因为这种疾病而衰竭。

sentences.en: But it might.
sentences.zh: 但它可能会。

sentences.en: And it might kill you.
sentences.zh: 而且它可能会要了你的命。

sentences.en: So, it's kind of like you're just walking around every day with a gun pointed to your head, never knowing if today's the day when it might go off.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就像你每天走在路上，头上都顶着一把枪，永远不知道今天会不会是扣动扳机的那一天。

sentences.en: Carl Zimmer writes about biology and genetics.
sentences.zh: Carl Zimmer 撰写关于生物学和遗传学的文章。

sentences.en: This disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, is caused by genes.
sentences.zh: 这种疾病，肥厚型心肌病，是由基因引起的。

sentences.en: In other words, if you inherit a gene with a mutation on it, you're going to make some of the proteins in your heart in a sort of defective way.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你遗传了一个带有突变的基因，你心脏中的某些蛋白质就会以一种有缺陷的方式制造出来。

sentences.en: And so, it's just something you're born with.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是你与生俱来的东西。

sentences.en: And it sounds like you're stuck with it.
sentences.zh: 听起来你只能认命了。

sentences.en: There's no cure.
sentences.zh: 没有治愈方法。

sentences.en: Because in order to cure it, you would actually have to go into people's DNA and rewrite it.
sentences.zh: 因为要治愈它，你实际上必须进入人们的 DNA 并重写它。

sentences.en: Last week, a group of scientists published a breakthrough that could do just that.
sentences.zh: 上周，一组科学家发表了一项突破性成果，可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: Edit and rewrite the gene that causes this heart condition.
sentences.zh: 编辑并重写导致这种心脏病的基因。

sentences.en: American scientists, for the first time, have successfully eliminated a genetic disease from human embryos.
sentences.zh: 美国科学家首次成功地从人类胚胎中消除了这种遗传病。

sentences.en: Genetic engineering yesterday was science fiction, and today it's reality.
sentences.zh: 昨天的基因工程是科幻小说，而今天它已成为现实。

sentences.en: The research targeted a heart defect, but experts say in the future, the same approach could potentially prevent a whole list of inheritable diseases.
sentences.zh: 这项研究针对的是一种心脏缺陷，但专家表示，未来这种方法可能预防一系列遗传性疾病。

sentences.en: Carl Zimmer, with this warning in mind that my scientific background is shallow, how exactly does one edit a gene?
sentences.zh: Carl Zimmer，考虑到我的科学背景很浅薄，到底该如何编辑基因？

sentences.en: Well, this recent breakthrough is an application of a new kind of tool for rewriting DNA called CRISPR.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最近的这一突破是 CRISPR 这种重写 DNA 的新工具的应用。

sentences.en: So, what scientists did was they created an embryo that had this disease.
sentences.zh: 所以，科学家们所做的是创造了一个患有这种疾病的胚胎。

sentences.en: In other words, one copy of a gene for a heart protein was faulty.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，心脏蛋白基因的一个拷贝是有缺陷的。

sentences.en: They added in molecules to this embryo, which were able to zero in on the part of the gene where this mutation was that causes the disease.
sentences.zh: 他们在胚胎中加入了分子，这些分子能够锁定基因中导致疾病的突变部分。

sentences.en: It's like they're paging through an incredibly long encyclopedia until they get to a particular page,
sentences.zh: 就像他们在翻阅一本极其厚重的百科全书，直到找到特定的一页，

sentences.en: and on that particular page, they get to a particular paragraph, and in that particular paragraph, they get to a particular word.
sentences.zh: 在那一页上，他们找到特定的段落，而在那个段落中，他们找到特定的单词。

sentences.en: They can zero in with that kind of incredible accuracy, and then what they do is they then cut a section of the DNA right there.
sentences.zh: 他们可以以那种令人难以置信的精确度锁定目标，然后他们就在那里切断一段 DNA。

sentences.en: Scientists can then insert a new piece of DNA to take its place.
sentences.zh: 科学家随后可以插入一段新的 DNA 来代替它。

sentences.en: So, they're removing a word in this deep well of language, and they're actually replacing it with another one.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们是在这深奥的生命语言中删掉一个词，并用另一个词来替换它。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, then what this cell did was it repaired the DNA, and in the process, it turned this gene into a normal version that you and I have that lets us have normal beating hearts.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个细胞随后修复了 DNA，在这个过程中，它把这个基因变成了你我都有的正常版本，让我们拥有正常跳动的心脏。

sentences.en: And so, if this embryo were to become a fully formed human, it would be a human without this terrible disease.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果这个胚胎发育成一个完整的人，他将是一个没有这种可怕疾病的人。

sentences.en: It would be eradicated from the biology of the baby and the adult.
sentences.zh: 它将从婴儿和成人的生物学中被彻底根除。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is truly revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 这确实是革命性的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's no exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这毫不夸张。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, Carl, tell me about the researcher behind this breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 那么，Carl，跟我说说这项突破背后的研究人员吧。

sentences.en: The researcher's name is Shukrat Metalipov.
sentences.zh: 这位研究人员的名字叫 Shukrat Metalipov。

sentences.en: First name is Shukrat, and last name is Metalipov.
sentences.zh: 名字是 Shukrat，姓是 Metalipov。

sentences.en: He grew up in the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 他在苏联长大。

sentences.en: In Kazakhstan.
sentences.zh: 在哈萨克斯坦。

sentences.en: Used to be a part of the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 曾经是苏联的一部分。

sentences.en: Became interested in studying the cells and embryos when he was in graduate school in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 他在莫斯科读研究生时开始对研究细胞和胚胎产生兴趣。

sentences.en: And I graduated with straight A's.
sentences.zh: 我以全优成绩毕业。

sentences.en: Then he came to the United States, started to work with a mentor.
sentences.zh: 然后他来到美国，开始与一位导师共事。

sentences.en: Keith Campbell.
sentences.zh: 基思·坎贝尔。

sentences.en: A scientist who had helped to create the first cloned animals, Dolly the Sheep.
sentences.zh: 一位帮助创造了第一批克隆动物——多莉羊的科学家。

sentences.en: I remember.
sentences.zh: 我记得。

sentences.en: Her name is Dolly.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫多莉。

sentences.en: Seven months old.
sentences.zh: 七个月大。

sentences.en: She may not be the monster imagined in a science fiction fantasy.
sentences.zh: 她可能并非科幻小说中想象的那种怪物。

sentences.en: So many scientists doubted it could ever be done.
sentences.zh: 许多科学家曾怀疑这是否真的能实现。

sentences.en: I was really shocked.
sentences.zh: 我当时真的很震惊。

sentences.en: So, this was kind of a big moment for me to understand that we have more power in manipulating nature than we think.
sentences.zh: 所以，对我来说，这是一个重要的时刻，让我意识到我们在操纵自然方面的能力比我们想象的要大。

sentences.en: For him, what was really important was that this could be a way to cure genetic diseases.
sentences.zh: 对他而言，真正重要的是这可能成为治愈遗传疾病的一种途径。

sentences.en: What Metalipov got famous for, first of all, was that he did research on what came to be known as three-parent babies.
sentences.zh: Metalipov 最初成名是因为他开展了后来被称为“三亲婴儿”的研究。

sentences.en: Whoa, whoa, whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇，等等，等等。

sentences.en: What is a three-parent baby?
sentences.zh: 什么是“三亲婴儿”？

sentences.en: It's an idea that bends the mind as well as the established laws of nature.
sentences.zh: 这是一个既挑战思维又挑战既定自然法则的概念。

sentences.en: One baby with three genetic parents.
sentences.zh: 一个拥有三个遗传学父母的婴儿。

sentences.en: It's sort of a label that got stuck on what is actually a way to try to treat really serious diseases.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个被贴在某种试图治疗严重疾病的方法上的标签。

sentences.en: Thirteen-month-old Jessica Newell suffers from a mitochondrial disease passed down from her mother.
sentences.zh: 13个月大的Jessica Newell患有一种从她母亲那里遗传来的线粒体疾病。

sentences.en: And doctors say things will get progressively worse.
sentences.zh: 医生说病情会逐渐恶化。

sentences.en: We only inherit our mitochondria from our mothers.
sentences.zh: 我们的线粒体只遗传自母亲。

sentences.en: And if there's a mutation in one of those genes, it can actually cause really severe diseases.
sentences.zh: 如果这些基因中存在突变，实际上会导致非常严重的疾病。

sentences.en: Scientists combined the DNA of two parents with the healthy mitochondria DNA of a female donor.
sentences.zh: 科学家们将父母双方的DNA与一名女性捐赠者的健康线粒体DNA结合起来。

sentences.en: And so, that's where you get three parents from.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是“三个父母”的由来。

sentences.en: Understood.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, what happened with that research, this three-parent baby concept?
sentences.zh: 那么，那项研究，即“三亲婴儿”的概念，后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: It worked in mice.
sentences.zh: 它在小鼠身上成功了。

sentences.en: And so, then Metalipov moved on to monkeys, which are closer to humans.
sentences.zh: 于是，Metalipov 转向了与人类更接近的猴子。

sentences.en: There were two baby monkeys that were born that were cured of their mitochondrial disease.
sentences.zh: 有两只猴宝宝出生了，它们的线粒体疾病得到了治愈。

sentences.en: So, that gave him and others sort of the boost to say,
sentences.zh: 这给了他和其他人一种推动力，让他们觉得：

sentences.en: OK, well, let's go to government agencies and ask for permission to move on to humans.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们去政府机构申请许可，进入人体试验阶段。

sentences.en: So, what happened when they went to these government agencies?
sentences.zh: 那么，当他们去这些政府机构时发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, in the United States, they got a big fat no.
sentences.zh: 在美国，他们得到了一个响亮的拒绝。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Do not do it.
sentences.zh: 不准做。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不行。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: The United States has been opposed to genetic modifications in human embryos for quite a long time.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，美国一直反对对人类胚胎进行基因改造。

sentences.en: They have made it very clear that they are not going to approve clinical trials.
sentences.zh: 他们已经明确表示不会批准临床试验。

sentences.en: In 2016, Congress inserted a little line into the budget, basically saying that the FDA cannot even consider an application for mitochondrial replacement therapy.
sentences.zh: 2016年，国会在预算案中加入了一条简短的条款，基本上规定FDA甚至不能考虑线粒体置换疗法的申请。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, an outright ban.
sentences.zh: 所以，是彻底的禁令。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's frustrating because, you know, this is the goal of my career is to bring new revolutionary treatments.
sentences.zh: 这很令人沮丧，因为你知道，我职业生涯的目标就是带来革命性的新疗法。

sentences.en: We invested so much into the science and we made so much progress.
sentences.zh: 我们投入了大量资金进行科学研究，也取得了很大进展。

sentences.en: And now, all suddenly, FDA was told not to continue this work.
sentences.zh: 而现在，FDA突然被告知不能继续这项工作。

sentences.en: So, where is this research being done?
sentences.zh: 那么，这项研究现在是在哪里进行的？

sentences.en: Well, in the United Kingdom, actually, they have gone forward with approving it.
sentences.zh: 实际上，在英国，他们已经批准了这项研究。

sentences.en: And so, they are moving forward with this, full steam ahead with lots of regulations and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们正在全力推进，并制定了大量的法规等等。

sentences.en: In the United States, it's just a very different story.
sentences.zh: 而在美国，情况则完全不同。

sentences.en: So, what happened with the three-parent baby, how that research stalled out in the U.S., feels like a cautionary tale of what could happen to Metalipov's latest research.
sentences.zh: 所以，“三亲婴儿”的研究在美国陷入停滞的经历，感觉就像是一个警示故事，预示着Metalipov最新的研究可能会遭遇什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I understand that we need to draw a line, what's permissible, what's not.
sentences.zh: 我理解我们需要划定界限，明确什么是允许的，什么是不允许的。

sentences.en: We don't want unregulated use.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望出现不受监管的使用。

sentences.en: But what we're asking is, let us test it.
sentences.zh: 但我们要求的是，让我们进行测试。

sentences.en: It needs to be tested in clinical settings.
sentences.zh: 它需要在临床环境中进行测试。

sentences.en: The scientists themselves have been kind of stunned by how fast they've been hitting these successes.
sentences.zh: 科学家们自己也对他们取得成功的速度感到震惊。

sentences.en: And so, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，

sentences.en: a lot of scientists are really making an effort to try to make the rest of us aware of what CRISPR is and what the potential benefits are and what the ethical issues are and so on.
sentences.zh: 许多科学家确实在努力让大众了解什么是CRISPR，它的潜在益处是什么，以及涉及的伦理问题等等。

sentences.en: I don't think, you know, this technology can be stopped at this stage.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这项技术在现阶段是可以被阻止的。

sentences.en: And I believe this is going to be the future.
sentences.zh: 我相信这就是未来。

sentences.en: And this is going to be in national interest of every country.
sentences.zh: 而且这符合每个国家的国家利益。

sentences.en: So, I think the United States have to just reconsider the policies.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为美国必须重新考虑其政策。

sentences.en: It's interesting because it feels like this technology is a bit like the Internet or like a big idea that it would be difficult to contain within one country or to keep out of another country,
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为这项技术感觉有点像互联网，或者像一个巨大的理念，很难将其限制在一个国家之内，或者阻止它进入另一个国家，

sentences.en: whether a government wants it to be kept out or not, right?
sentences.zh: 无论政府是否希望阻止它，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it will be kind of normalized over time.
sentences.zh: 因为它会随着时间的推移而变得常态化。

sentences.en: Is that your sense?
sentences.zh: 你是这样认为的吗？

sentences.en: It's really hard for me to look into the future on this one because when you look at, you know, our past experiences,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，很难预测这方面的未来，因为当你回顾我们过去的经历时，

sentences.en: sometimes things go from being really shocking and horrifying to normal.
sentences.zh: 有时事情会从令人震惊和恐惧变得习以为常。

sentences.en: And in vitro fertilization in the 1960s was really considered very scandalous.
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代的体外受精技术曾被认为是非常丑闻的。

sentences.en: Most people were against it if you asked them in a poll.
sentences.zh: 如果你在民意调查中询问，大多数人都是反对的。

sentences.en: Because it was seen as a manipulation of life.
sentences.zh: 因为它被视为对生命的操纵。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We did not have the right to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们没有权利那样做。

sentences.en: And now it's incredibly common practice.
sentences.zh: 而现在，这已成为极其普遍的做法。

sentences.en: Extremely common, yes.
sentences.zh: 非常普遍，是的。

sentences.en: Regulated.
sentences.zh: 受到监管。

sentences.en: It's licensed in the United States and so on.
sentences.zh: 它在美国等地已获得许可。

sentences.en: And so it's just a familiar part of life.
sentences.zh: 所以它只是生活中熟悉的一部分。

sentences.en: So, you know, the question is, will CRISPR become a familiar part of life 50 years from now?
sentences.zh: 所以，问题是，50年后CRISPR会成为生活中熟悉的一部分吗？

sentences.en: I really don't know.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道。

sentences.en: So, you said this is truly revolutionary in the world of science and medicine.
sentences.zh: 你说这在科学和医学界是真正革命性的。

sentences.en: Why is it such a big deal?
sentences.zh: 为什么它如此重要？

sentences.en: You know, scientists have wanted to do this for decades.
sentences.zh: 你知道，科学家们几十年来一直想做这件事。

sentences.en: Fix genetic diseases by manipulating embryos.
sentences.zh: 通过操纵胚胎来修复遗传疾病。

sentences.en: These embryos, they looked like normal embryos.
sentences.zh: 这些胚胎看起来就像正常的胚胎。

sentences.en: In other words, it's possible that if you took one of these embryos, implanted it in a surrogate mother,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你取出一个这样的胚胎，植入代孕母亲体内，

sentences.en: the embryo would develop into a normal human being, healthy despite having edited DNA.
sentences.zh: 这个胚胎可能会发育成一个正常的人类，尽管编辑过DNA，但依然健康。

sentences.en: And, in fact, would not carry the disease that they had inherited.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它不会携带它们原本遗传的疾病。

sentences.en: And not only that, but would not pass it down to their descendants.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，也不会将疾病传给后代。

sentences.en: I know in the future, these type of treatments will become routine.
sentences.zh: 我知道在未来，这类治疗将成为常规。

sentences.en: Probably a million children will be cured of these heritable conditions.
sentences.zh: 可能有数百万儿童将从这些遗传性疾病中治愈。

sentences.en: And that's what motivates me every day.
sentences.zh: 这就是我每天工作的动力。

sentences.en: I didn't want to be an ordinary scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 我不想成为一个普通的科学家。

sentences.en: But I want the best of the beSt.
sentences.zh: 我要成为最顶尖的人。

sentences.en: I want to be number one.
sentences.zh: 我想成为第一名。

sentences.en: And hopefully, I'll show everybody that they are wrong.
sentences.zh: 希望我能向所有人证明他们是错的。

sentences.en: A hundred years from now, they're going to remember, yep, that guy developed it.
sentences.zh: 一百年后，人们会记得，没错，就是那个人开发了它。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的消息。

sentences.en: The present first lady are absolutely fully engaged on a tragedy that is crossing the country.
sentences.zh: 总统和第一夫人正全力应对一场席卷全国的悲剧。

sentences.en: The Trump administration says it plans to use all the resources of the federal government
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府表示，计划动用联邦政府的所有资源，

sentences.en: to confront the opioid epidemic that has claimed tens of thousands of lives, calling it an emergency.
sentences.zh: 来对抗已夺去数万人生命的阿片类药物流行病，并称其为紧急状态。

sentences.en: The best way to prevent drug addiction and overdose is to prevent people from abusing drugs in the first place.
sentences.zh: 预防药物成瘾和过量用药的最佳方法，是从源头上防止人们滥用药物。

sentences.en: The president himself addressed the issue from Bedminster.
sentences.zh: 总统本人在贝德明斯特谈到了这个问题。

sentences.en: If they don't start, they won't have a problem.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不开始，就不会有问题。

sentences.en: If they do start, it's awfully tough to get off.
sentences.zh: 如果他们一旦开始，就很难戒掉。

sentences.en: So we can keep them from going on and maybe by talking to youth and telling them no good, really bad for you in every way.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以阻止他们尝试，也许通过与年轻人交谈，告诉他们这没有任何好处，在各方面对你都非常有害。

sentences.en: But if they don't start, it will never be a problem.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们不开始，这就永远不会成为问题。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《The Daily》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbola.
sentences.zh: 我是Michael Barbola。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时甚至令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《Metro》中，我和Sarah Koenig将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在任何你收听播客的地方订阅。

sentences.en: Be prepared.
sentences.zh: 做好准备。

sentences.en: Man onwomen.
sentences.zh: 男人对女人。

sentences.en: Man on son.
sentences.zh: 男人对儿子。
